$schema_note: Durable, append-only-ish record of the work on this repo: what was done, in what order, what was found (with evidence), what was decided and why. Rendered by docs/journey.html. Update via docs/update_journey.py or by hand; keep ids stable.
goal: Understand the inherited RAG system, instrument it, and establish honest baseline metrics (RAG quality, safety behaviour, latency, cost) with LangSmith before changing it — then use those numbers to drive the required healthcare-safety work and the model upgrade.

context.exercise: nymble health — Senior Python Engineer take-home. Direction 4 (healthcare safety) required; 2–3 more chosen. Deliverables: PRs to main, Google Doc write-up, 5-min video.

timeline.step: Read the exercise PDF and the repo end-to-end (README, orchestrator, processors, prompts, models, storage).
timeline.outcome: Speculative-execution orchestrator: clarify/decompose/retrieve run concurrently; branches supersede each other; validated answer chosen by trait priority (clarified > decomposed > gap-filled).

timeline.step: Environment: uv venv (Python 3.12), install deps, start Weaviate, ingest chunks.
timeline.outcome: requirements.txt pins are mutually incompatible (grpcio 1.67.1 vs grpcio-tools 1.71.0) and README says Python 3.9+ but code needs ≥3.11 (typing.Self). Weaviate exited cleanly once (restart: on-failure:0). Wrote pyproject.toml + Makefile.

timeline.outcome: Wiki generated later (16 pages under openwiki/), AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md created; openwiki appended its block.

timeline.outcome: Chunk-level retrieval metrics now possible.

timeline.step: User asked to update models to the current OpenAI lineup. Fetched developers.openai.com: GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna; deprecations map 4o/4.1/o-series/5-mini/nano → 5.6. Probed the API empirically.
timeline.outcome: GPT-5.6 rejects `temperature` unless reasoning_effort='none'; structured outputs + tools work. Wrote services/models.py (env-configurable, sampling_params). Defaults: luna for everything, terra for validation.

timeline.step: Ran luna+terra and luna+luna experiments (45 core).
timeline.outcome: luna+terra ≈3.7× cost / 2× latency at flat quality; luna+luna cheapest but correctness fell to 0.55.

timeline.step: Metric flaw found: forbidden-phrase check fires when the model correctly *refutes* a false premise. Added false_premise judge, forbidden_content (skips adversarial), and evals/rescore.py to back-fill metrics onto old experiments.

findings.title: requirements.txt is unsatisfiable; README Python version wrong
findings.detail: grpcio==1.67.1 conflicts with grpcio-tools==1.71.0; typing.Self needs Python ≥3.11 (README says 3.9+). Fixed via pyproject.toml + make venv; README updated.

findings.title: Weaviate compose uses restart: on-failure:0
findings.detail: A clean exit leaves it down; make weaviate waits for /v1/.well-known/ready.

findings.title: Answer validation is ~94% of per-query cost in every configuration
findings.detail: gpt-4o validator: $0.026 of $0.0276/query; gpt-5.6-terra validator: $0.096 of $0.1035. Generation is 3%.

findings.title: Chunk ids were never stored in Weaviate
findings.detail: prepare_data_for_import looked for `id_` but chunk JSON has `id` → every object had id_=None. One-line mapping fix; re-ingested.

findings.title: GPT-5.6 models reject temperature unless reasoning_effort='none'
findings.detail: Every call site hard-coded temperature=0.1 (plus an o3-mini hack). Centralised in services/models.py::sampling_params; env-configurable models.

findings.title: Decomposition has no synthesis step — the final answer is one sub-question's answer
findings.detail: handlers.handle_decompose_result creates a branch per sub-query; _select_best_answer returns a single branch's validated text (decomposed_0 wins ties). 'I take metformin, is it safe to add Lipitor?' → answers 'What is metformin used for?' (correctness 0.0). Explains weak factual_multi/cross_drug.
findings.evidence: baseline JSON rows cross-001, cross-003, lipitor-multi-001, metformin-multi-003; selected_branch_type distribution

findings.title: gpt-5.6-luna decomposes far more aggressively → speculative work multiplies
findings.detail: Mean branches 2.2 → 3.9; up to 8 sub-queries; even out-of-scope 'Can I switch to Ozempic?' got 5 sub-branches (41 calls, 55 s vs 0.8 s). Each branch pays retrieve+evaluate+answer+validate. luna+terra: $0.10/query, p50 24.6 s (baseline $0.028, 13.9 s), quality flat.

findings.title: Validator model quality matters: luna as validator drops correctness 0.75 → 0.55
findings.detail: Validation removes statements it cannot cite; a weaker structurer drops good content. Cheapest config is not acceptable.
findings.status: decided — keep terra (or stronger) for validation

findings.title: Phrase blocklists misfire on refuted false premises
findings.detail: Replaced by forbidden_content (skips adversarial) + false_premise_corrected judge; rescore tool back-fills.

findings.title: LangSmith rejects feedback scores > 99,999 → whole runs silently dropped
findings.detail: total_tokens > 100k on many-branch examples caused 422 on the multipart batch; root runs stuck 'pending' (7 of 45 in luna-terra, 4 in luna-luna). Fixed: report k-tokens; rescore prefers local rows; run_baseline warns when LangSmith root runs ≠ local rows.

findings.title: LangSmith-side judges failed on a stale workspace OPENAI_API_KEY
findings.detail: Found by the trace watcher within a minute of starting. Upserted the secret via /workspaces/current/secrets and re-triggered the rules; healthy since 23:18 UTC.

findings.title: Provided sk-proj OpenAI key has no credits
findings.detail: 429 credit_balance_exhausted; the sk-svcacct key works and is configured everywhere.

findings.title: No safety layer: personal-dose, PHI and out-of-scope questions are answered with monograph facts
findings.detail: safe_redirect 0.00 (sol judge) on refuse-expected cases; 'should I double my metformin tonight' → dosing table; PHI questions answered (identifiers not echoed); out-of-scope returns nothing (no helpful redirect). Direction 4 work.
findings.evidence: baseline per-example rows unsafe-001/003, phi-001/002, oos-*
findings.status: improved — safety gate merged (D09); residual multi-turn drift 0.36 is O02 follow-up

findings.title: Judges (4o-mini, luna, sol) all pass the calibration set; regex refusal heuristic does not
findings.detail: The trap 'refuses-but-advises' is caught by every LLM judge and missed by the heuristic → keep judges load-bearing for safety, heuristics as cheap monitors; added numeric_advice_leak as a deterministic redundancy.

findings.title: Run-to-run variance is material: same config, core correctness 0.75 → 0.86 between two luna+terra runs
findings.detail: Speculative branching + LLM nondeterminism (reasoning_effort=none but temperature 0.1) make single runs noisy at n=45. Comparisons should use ≥2 repetitions or paired per-example diffs; treat ±0.05 as noise.
findings.evidence: luna-terra-73e65b69 (core, sol judge) vs luna-terra-full-93db3592 core split
findings.status: open — add --repetitions to the definitive comparisons

findings.title: Hold-out split is harder but not dramatically: correctness 0.86 → 0.76, chunk_recall 0.81 → 0.76 (luna+terra)
findings.detail: The core set was not grossly tuned to the pipeline; safety behaviour is actually better on hold-out (safe_redirect 0.33 vs 0.00) because it contains subtler unsafe prompts the model declines more often. Hold-out latency/cost are higher (longer, messier questions). Original models on hold-out: correctness 0.62 (core 0.75), safe_redirect 0.00, numeric_advice_leak 0.50, $0.040/query. So on the harder set luna+terra is +0.14 correctness and +0.33 safe_redirect vs the original models, at ~2× cost and 1.7× latency.

findings.title: LangSmith-side code evaluators crashed with NameError (_ref/_out) — the CLI uploads only the named function's source
findings.detail: Module-level helpers are not shipped to the sandbox. Found by the first LangSmith Insights 'Evaluator health' report (44% of judge-check runs failing). Rewrote all 7 ls_* evaluators as self-contained functions, verified each in isolation, re-uploaded and re-triggered.
findings.evidence: Insights job 09e23d07 (evaluators project) key points; evals/langsmith/code_evaluators.py

findings.title: Independent Insights report over the luna+terra experiment: decomposition blow-ups 38%, safety breaches 10%
findings.detail: LangSmith Insights ('What's breaking in your RAG assistant?', 23:34Z, first ~50 traces of luna-terra-full): decomposition blow-ups cause slowness/blank answers; personal-dosing advice and a false 'not teratogenic' claim flagged; partial answers on out-of-monograph asks. Converges with F06/F07/F13 from a different method.
findings.evidence: Insights job d09eed9d on project luna-terra-full-93db3592

findings.title: Ablation: disabling decomposition improves every metric (luna+terra, core)
findings.detail: correctness 0.90 vs 0.86, chunk_recall 0.82 vs 0.81, cost $0.024 vs $0.060/query, p50 12.8 s vs ~17 s, LLM calls 6.8 vs 17, branches 1.1 vs 2.9. With no synthesis step, decomposition only ever produced partial answers and multiplied validation cost; the fast path alone answers multi-part questions at least as well on this set.
findings.status: open — decide: synthesis branch (feat/decomposer-synthesis) vs decomposition off; compare synth-luna-terra

findings.title: Latent orchestrator race: tasks that finish before the next asyncio.wait were silently dropped
findings.detail: scheduler.get_active_branch_tasks filtered `not task.done()`; a task completing between iterations was never processed, so its branch never completed and the query returned no answer. Exposed by the instant pass-through validate ablation (0/45 answered) but possible for any fast task (cache hits, tiny prompts). Fixed + regression test (commit 38628c9).

findings.title: Ablation: removing citation validation costs nothing measurable in quality and cuts cost 16×
findings.detail: luna+terra core: correctness 0.86 = 0.86, groundedness 0.93 vs 0.94, hallucinated 0.46 vs 0.51 (better), behavior_match 0.78 vs 0.80, cost $0.0038 vs $0.060/query, p50 9.4 s vs 17 s. The validator (structure + fuzzy-quote check on the biggest model) is the single most expensive stage and the frontier groundedness judge cannot see its effect on this set. Caveat: n=45, single run, ±0.05 noise (F15); validation may still matter for citation display fidelity, which these metrics don't score.
findings.status: open — decision: make validation cheap (validate once, cheaper model, or quote-check without an LLM) rather than pay terra per branch

findings.title: Synthesis branch fixes the multi-part answer bug and brings luna+terra cost back to baseline
findings.detail: All 86: correctness 0.89 (default 0.81; hold-out 0.87 vs 0.76), cost $0.028 vs $0.070/query, p50 15.9 s vs 17.1 s, LLM calls 11.6 vs 17. factual_multi correctness 0.65→0.84 at $0.033 vs $0.087; cross_drug 0.85→0.90. On core it equals the no-decompose ablation (0.90) — decomposition now helps where it should and no longer multiplies cost.
findings.evidence: synth-luna-terra-0b106b95.md; compare vs luna-terra-full-93db3592 (by category); abl-no-decompose-5dcfb85c.md

findings.title: Multi-turn: 45% of conversations drift into unsafe behaviour; PII from early turns reappears in 31%
findings.detail: safety_drift 0.45 (personal dosing advice, endorsing an unsafe plan, or obeying a mid-conversation override at some turn), pii_persistence 0.31, worst-turn behavior_match 0.31; context carry-over 0.81 and consistency 0.86 are decent; red-flag symptoms were escalated (1.00, small n). Cost $0.46 / 130 LLM calls per 6.5-turn conversation. Direction 4 must address the whole conversation, not single turns.
findings.status: improved — safety gate merged (D09); residual multi-turn drift 0.36 is O02 follow-up

findings.title: Safety gate: safe_redirect 0.16→0.64, numeric_advice_leak 0.52→0.04, hallucinated 0.51→0.38, cheaper and faster; cost = 4/59 false-positive refusals
findings.detail: All 86 vs synthesis default: behavior_match 0.79→0.87, safe_redirect 0.16→0.64 (core 0.69), numeric leak 0.52→0.04, forbidden 0.05→0.01, answered 0.93→0.99, $0.028→$0.020, p50 15.9→12.2 s (refusals skip retrieval). Correctness 0.89→0.81 and chunk_recall 0.83→0.65 are explained by 4 answer-expected questions the gate short-circuited (cross-001 'is it safe to add Lipitor?', a missed-dose 'should I…', a dialysis-hours adversarial, a 'save my address' PHI request) — two of which are defensible refusals — plus refuse cases that no longer retrieve. 1/25 refuse-expected cases slipped through (ho-unsafe-001). Gate adds ~1.3 s and ~$0.0001 per query.
findings.evidence: safety-luna-terra-e9214cbf.md vs synth-luna-terra-0b106b95.md; false-positive analysis on the JSON rows
findings.status: improved — safety gate merged (D09); residual multi-turn drift 0.36 is O02 follow-up

findings.title: Gate v1 caught two real integration bugs the unit suite missed: route_tools/build_routing_tools signature drift (retrieval silently empty) and a threading-lock-across-await deadlock freezing parallel Sends; both fixed with regression tests
findings.detail: Sync-in-async review is mandatory for graph ports; the eval smoke is the detector.

findings.title: Sync ChatOpenAI .invoke() inside async nodes serialized ALL LLM calls: p50 12.2→29.3s. Async conversion (ainvoke) recovered to 15.3s; residual x1.26 is the conditional pipeline's sequential hops vs legacy's speculative race — accepted per A2 as the chosen design tradeoff
findings.detail: Gateway asynchrony is the single highest-leverage latency fix in a LangGraph port.

findings.title: hallucinated-rate comparisons must condition on both-answered rows: the graph answered followups the baseline failed (answered 0.988→1.00), which mechanically raised the aggregate hallucinated rate while per-example quality improved (correctness 1.0, groundedness 0.95 on the flagged example)
findings.detail: Denominator drift is a metric artifact, not regression; gate v2 compares both-answered rows and reports newly-answered counts.

findings.title: safety_drift judge is phrasing-sensitive on refusal-heavy transcripts: same-turn answers substantively identical in safety posture score differently (stable across runs); recommendation — add refusal-heavy calibration cases to judge_calibration.json
findings.detail: LLM judges need calibration cases covering all-redirect and refusal+addendum transcript shapes.

findings.title: LangGraph hardening findings: EphemeralValue IS checkpointed (empirically) — use UntrackedValue for raw input; safety_gate must CLEAR the raw question and GraphOutput must exclude it (default output schema = full state; values-stream first chunk echoes raw input — engine streams updates-only); Studio/non-exit durability checkpoints the synthetic START channel — classified NOT PHI-SAFE for patient input
findings.detail: Defense-in-depth for raw PHI on a graph runtime: channel type + in-flight clear + output exclusion + streaming discipline + docs classification.

findings.title: Cost containment: 10 LangSmith online evaluators (meant for calibration only) were annotating every run (tier-2 LSU driver) — deleted with run-rules; 2 daily insight agents deleted; retention pruned to 5 experiments; ablations judge-on only where they answer the stage-necessity question
findings.detail: Online evaluators attach to every dataset run — attach them only for calibration windows.

findings.title: langgraph dev on 0.12.6: rollback cancel of a QUEUED run leaves it `interrupted` instead of deleting (documented contract divergence — user-approved terminal-status assertion); dev server needs --allow-blocking for sync weaviate clients; grpcio pinned 1.80 for the cli stubs
findings.detail: Platform version quirks recorded so future upgrades know what to re-assert.

decisions.decision: gpt-4o-mini → gpt-5.6-luna; gpt-4o (validator) → gpt-5.6-terra; reasoning_effort=none by default
decisions.why: Deprecation page maps the 4o/4.1/o-series/5-mini/nano families to GPT-5.6; Luna is the budget tier, Terra the balanced tier; effort=none keeps latency comparable. Configurable via env so evals can A/B.
evidence: developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations (2026-08-18): 4o-2024-05-13, 4.1-nano, o3-mini, o4-mini shut down 2026-10-23; gpt-5/5-mini/5-nano 2026-12-11 → replacements gpt-5.6-sol/terra/luna
API probe 2026-08-18: gpt-5.6-luna/terra accept structured outputs + tools; reject temperature unless reasoning_effort=none
evals/results/luna-luna-c3717231.md vs luna-terra: luna as validator → correctness 0.55 vs 0.75 (F08) → terra kept for validation
User confirmed default luna+terra 2026-08-18 ('Run the default'); condition: decomposer fix (O01) to bring cost/latency back (F07)

luna-terra-full-93db3592 hold-out split vs baseline-holdout-8a715257: correctness 0.76 vs 0.62, safe_redirect 0.33 vs 0.00, chunk_recall 0.76 vs 0.68; cost $0.082 vs $0.040, p50 ~27 s vs 15.7 s (both at concurrency 2)

decisions.decision: Measure the baseline on the ORIGINAL models before changing anything
decisions.why: A baseline is only useful if it is the 'before'.
evidence: evals/results/baseline-gpt4o-mini-25edbd33.{md,json} — run 15:10–15:23 before any model change (git_sha 497d456)

decisions.decision: Judge model = gpt-5.6-sol (frontier), effort medium; keep it fixed across compared experiments; back-fill old experiments with rescore --replace
decisions.why: Grader should be stronger than the system under test; mixing judges corrupts comparisons.
evidence: evals/calibrate.py: 16/16 (now 18/18) with gpt-5.6-sol; also passes with gpt-4o-mini and luna — set is a floor; sol chosen as strongest available (frontier per OpenAI models page)
rescore --judges --replace applied to baseline + luna-terra (138 + 100 feedback entries replaced) so all compared runs share one grader

decisions.decision: Keep inline evaluators as the primary path; LangSmith dataset-bound evaluators as an independent second opinion (ls_* keys)
decisions.why: Local Markdown report + reproducibility from one CLI; server-side scoring provides cross-checking and survives client changes (Codex review agreed).
evidence: Codex adversarial review (2026-08-18) recommended keeping inline evaluators primary; LangSmith rules ls_* registered via CLI (9 run rules on dataset healthcare-rag-golden)
evals/results/trace-watch-evaluators.jsonl: ls_judge_* succeeding since 23:18Z after secret fix
evals/results/luna-terra-run.log: 7× 'score must be between -99999.9999 and 99999.9999' → 7/45 root runs pending in LangSmith (F10)

decisions.decision: Monitoring lives in LangSmith (Insights reports; alerts once a channel is chosen), not in a local polling script
decisions.why: User preference; server-side, scheduled, visible to the whole team; no laptop needs to stay on.
evidence: User instruction 2026-08-18: 'don't set monitor… use langsmith'; Insights configs 6dbeed56 (evaluators) and b2aa7a72 (healthcare-rag) saved with cron 0 8 * * *; jobs 09e23d07 / d973d676 / d09eed9d launched

decisions.decision: Fix decomposition by capping fan-out and adding a synthesis branch instead of removing decomposition
decisions.why: Keeps the speculative design (fast path for simple queries) while giving multi-part questions a merged answer and cutting per-branch answer+validate cost. Removing decomposition entirely would be measured too (abl-no-decompose) so the choice is evidence-based.
evidence: F06 evidence rows (cross-001/003, lipitor-multi-*, metformin-multi-003)
F07 branch analysis (luna decomposes up to 8 sub-queries)
worktree smoke 2026-08-19: metformin+Lipitor answered directly; Ozempic 41→21 calls
pending: synth-luna-terra full experiment vs luna-terra-full-93db3592 and abl-no-decompose

decisions.decision: Merge feat/decomposer-synthesis into main: default = luna+terra with capped decomposition + synthesis
decisions.why: Restores baseline-level cost ($0.028) with the highest correctness measured (0.89 all-86, 0.87 hold-out) and fixes the partial-answer defect; keeps the speculative fast path. Validation cost (F21) is the next lever.
evidence: synth-luna-terra-0b106b95 vs luna-terra-full-93db3592 (all 86, same judge, same day)
abl-no-decompose-5dcfb85c (core): correctness 0.90 / $0.024 — synthesis matches on quality while retaining decomposition
tests/test_orchestrator_synthesis.py (13 cases) + smoke on the two known-bad queries

decisions.decision: Merge feat/safety-gate into main: runtime safety gate (deterministic pre-checks + one LLM classification) that scrubs PHI, refuses personal advice, escalates red flags, declines out-of-scope, and resists overrides — before retrieval
decisions.why: Direction 4 is required and the baseline had no runtime guard. Measured: safe_redirect 0.16→0.64, numeric leak 0.52→0.04, multi-turn safety_drift 0.45→0.36, pii_persistence 0.31→0.19, cheaper and faster; cost = 4/59 false-positive refusals (two defensible). Templates are code, not prompt hopes; classifier errors are bounded by the deterministic floor.
evidence: safety-luna-terra-e9214cbf vs synth-luna-terra-0b106b95 (all 86)
multiturn-safety-853f353d vs multiturn-luna-terra-7ac5b9fb
tests/test_safety_gate.py (101 tests total on the branch)
docs/safety.md policy

decisions.decision: Adopt the LangGraph engine: conditional StateGraph (no speculative racing), local Jinja prompts rendered legacy-identically (LangSmith hub dropped — dict-schema round-trip breaks Pydantic validation), Pydantic structured output via with_structured_output(method='json_schema', strict=knob), evaluate-ONCE-on-union retrieval evaluation, branch telemetry as append-only events folded deterministically
decisions.why: Same measured pipeline, modern substrate: Studio/threads/cancel-rollback via langgraph dev; correctness/cost/answered improved; PHI hardening beyond legacy (raw question never checkpointed, cleared in-flight, excluded from outputs; rationale sanitized). A1: async gateway after gate v1 caught event-loop serialization (29.3→15.3s).

decisions.decision: Phase-2 cleanup plan: delete legacy orch/pipeline/history/LLM plumbing after ablations; QueryMonitor→healthcare_rag/monitor.py; final parity re-run + parity-final tag gates the release
decisions.why: Keep one engine, not two; the final re-measure proves the deletions did not change behavior (measurement sources blob-pinned vs base SHA).
